ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Joe Louis

code.originalText: Four-week review: psychotic symptoms, urine tests, blood pressure and a diagnosis of hypertension

text.paragraph: Four-week review: psychotic symptoms, urine tests and blood pressure. [S]

Mr. Louis returns four weeks after intake. About five days ago he noticed that he no longer believed he was being followed, and he now calls those fears part of the cocaine. He sleeps six to seven hours. In the first week of aripiprazole he felt a little restless in the evenings, which passed. All six contingency management urine tests have been negative, and he has drawn several prizes. He has had three therapy sessions and is working on what he does in the evenings and when he travels. His cold from the sick visit cleared within a week without a decongestant. His home blood pressure readings over the past week average 144/90. He met the social worker. He has signed a release allowing the clinic to talk with one family member he chose about his plan; no conversation has taken place yet. [S]

list.item:
Cocaine use disorder, severe, with cocaine-induced psychotic disorder (F14.250). The persecutory delusions resolved within about four weeks of abstinence and just over two weeks of aripiprazole, which supports a substance-induced psychosis rather than a primary psychotic disorder. Four weeks without cocaine, confirmed by six negative urine tests. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Continue aripiprazole 5 mg; a taper will be discussed after about six weeks of remission.
Continue contingency management and weekly therapy.

Hypertension, stage 2 (I10). Clinic 146/92 and home average 144/90 mmHg four weeks after his last cocaine use: stage 2 hypertension. Left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage on the intake ECG; urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 14 mg/g; creatinine and potassium normal at intake. [S]
Amlodipine 5 mg daily, with lifestyle changes: less salt, regular walks and less alcohol.
Echocardiogram for left ventricular hypertrophy, with measurement of the aortic root and ascending aorta.
Home readings continued; target below 130/80 mmHg.

Financial insecurity (Z59.86). The social worker is helping with a budget and has referred him to a Low Income Taxpayer Clinic to review his old tax records. [S]
Tax clinic appointment next month.
Check his eligibility for veterans' benefits.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (2020); Treatment for Stimulant Use Disorders (Treatment Improvement Protocol 33, updated 2021) (2021); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Preventive visit in five weeks. Ten-week review in six weeks with the echocardiogram that morning and the MoCA. Home readings daily for two weeks, then twice a week. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-14: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
